Identify the components present in the whiteboard diagram and described in the video transcript: EKS, EC2, NAT (NGW), NLB in the main VPC; TransitGateway (TRANSIT GW) acting as the hub; DirectConnect and VPN connecting to Transit Gateway; PrivateLink in the Shared Services VPC connected to Transit Gateway.

graph.name: Adobe Multi-VPC Architecture with AWS Transit Gateway
graph.notes: Adobe uses AWS Transit Gateway as a regional routing hub connecting thousands of product team VPCs, on-premise infrastructure via Direct Connect and VPN, and Shared Services using VPC PrivateLink.

nodes.name: EKS
nodes.notes: Deployed in local reused CIDR block.

nodes.name: EC2
nodes.notes: Deployed in local reused CIDR block.

nodes.name: NGW
nodes.notes: Deployed in routed CIDR block to perform NAT between private IPs.

nodes.name: NLB
nodes.notes: Deployed in routed CIDR block for inbound/routed traffic.

nodes.name: TRANSIT GW
nodes.notes: Regional routing hub interconnecting VPCs, Direct Connect, and VPNs.

nodes.name: DIRECT CONNECT
nodes.notes: Provides dedicated hybrid connectivity to Transit Gateway.

nodes.name: VPN
nodes.notes: Provides IPsec VPN connectivity to Transit Gateway.

nodes.name: VPC PRIVATE LINK
nodes.notes: Exposes shared service provider endpoints in the Shared Services VPC.

edges.notes: EKS cluster sends egress traffic to NAT Gateway.
NAT Gateway forwards NATed traffic to Transit Gateway.
Transit Gateway routes traffic to PrivateLink in the Shared Services VPC.
Direct Connect delivers on-prem traffic to Transit Gateway.
VPN delivers remote traffic to Transit Gateway.
